name: Mechanics of Biological Cells
description: This course focuses on cellular and sub-cellular level mechanics. We develop low-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics and stochastic transport to explain Brownian motion, diffusion, chemotaxis, and biased random walks, alongside active-matter models for actomyosin force generation, cortical tension, and membrane shape dynamics. Motility mechanisms such as amoeboid and mesenchymal crawling, actin-polymerization-based protrusion, flagellar and peristaltic body deformation-based swimming of micro-organisms in Newtonian fluids. Experimental labs will pertain to single-cell tracking, microfluidics, traction force microscopy, optical/magnetic tweezers, and AFM
